research_rationale:
EO 5881 (July 9, 1932), read in the official OFR 1974 Hoover PEO vol. II compilation (official_compilation_high, acceptable_as_original), is a single-clause order under section 204 of the Economy Act of June 30, 1932 further exempting William L. Hill, John Lewis May and Leonard Magruder (Treasury) from compulsory retirement 'and continued in the service until August 1, 1932', to afford time to appoint successors. It follows the earlier exemption order of June 30, 1932 recited in its text (whose exemption ran to July 10, 1932; that order's number is not in the project's identity universe, so it is not cited by number here). The order ends by its own terms on 1932-08-01. NOTE: the machine TERM record's stated_end_date (1932-07-10) misreads the recital of the earlier order's term; its span (chars 910-1759 of the held text) contains the operative words 'until August 1, 1932', which govern. Authority check: section 204 of Part II of the Legislative Appropriation Act of June 30, 1932 (Economy Act). No held source shows repeal or amendment of section 204 before this order's stated end date; the held WPA entries for EO 6615 (Feb. 26, 1934) and EO 6974/6975 (Feb. 1935) show the President still granting exemptions from the compulsory retirement provisions after this order's end, which corroborates that the statutory scheme (and so the exemption's object) continued through the stated date.
